keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1831-1833: the infobox gives 'Established: 20 October 1831' but Cliopatria's row begins in 1834, and the Gran Colombia dossier asks for a keyframe for the State of New Granada (1831) and the Republic (1832-1833), which no Cliopatria row covers. The outline is Cliopatria's 1834 shape, a unitary state consisting 'primarily of present-day Colombia and Panama' with smaller portions of Costa Rica, Ecuador, Venezuela, Peru and Brazil. The Gran Colombia dossier hands over only Colombia and Panama (about 1.2 M km2); the 1834 shape adds 0.2 M km2 of Amazon claims, which the page's list of neighbouring portions supports but does not date. [fx-44, R120: the Brazilian cells of the 1834 shape are cut here and in the 1834 keyframe.]

1,423,060 km2 for 1834-1852 against the infobox's 1,331,250 km2 (no year given for the figure): ratio 1.07. The shape holds Colombia and Panama plus 752 cells of Brazil's Amazonas, 27 of Peru's Loreto and slivers of Venezuela and Ecuador, consistent with the page's 'smaller portions' of five neighbours but undated. Panama tried to break away 'unsuccessfully' in 1840 and 1850; the War of the Supremes (1839) and the 1851 civil war moved no border. Unverified: page budget. [fx-44, R120: adjusted. Amazonas page (Brazilian state): the 'comarca of Rio Negro, the upper Amazon region, was incorporated into the Empire of Brazil in 1824'; 'In 1761, a fort was built on the location' (Sao Gabriel); the frontier in the north was settled only by 'the Treaty Vasquez Cobo-Martins (1908)', 'finally entitling those possessions in the north to Brazil'. The shape's 752 Brazilian cells (all Amazonas) are cut; the Republic of New Granada page lists 'smaller portions' of Brazil among its land without a date or extent, and Cliopatria drops 741 of the cells in 1853. Confidence 1: the pages give no extent for the 1830s-1850s claim; the cells are left to the Brazilian dossier (a handoff asks it to draw the upper Rio Negro).]

keyframe_review.note: 1,223,348 km2 for 1853-1856 (ratio 0.92 to the infobox): 199,712 km2 smaller than 1834-1852, losing 741 cells of Brazil's Amazonas and slices of Colombia's own Vaupes, Amazonas and Guainia. No page opened dates or explains a loss in 1853, and the republic page still lists portions of Brazil among its land, so the drop looks like a change in Cliopatria's claim rather than a treaty. The shape stands as the later, smaller one. In 1855-1857 'seven states were created out of the provinces' (a federal arrangement, not a loss of land); Panama is listed as a state from 27 February 1855 and the territories of Caqueta and San Andres were created on 15 June 1857 (Territorial evolution page).
Identical to 1853-1856 (1,223,348 km2) for 1857-1858. The republic was 'renamed into the Granadine Confederation' in 1858; Cliopatria's Granadine Confederation row begins in 1859.

ledger.note: 20 October 1831: the State of New Granada is created from the central departments of Gran Colombia. Infobox 'Established: 20 October 1831'; the Gran Colombia dossier dates the abolition of Gran Colombia to 21 November 1831. [fx-44, R120: found region cut to the same land as the 1831 and 1834 keyframes, so the keyframe does not release it.]

1858: New Granada becomes the Granadine Confederation. The page says the republic 'was renamed into the Granadine Confederation' in 1858, with a constitutional change dated 11 April 1858; Cliopatria starts the Confederation in 1859 on the same land.

wars.name: War of the Supremes
wars.outcome: A dispute over the dissolution of monasteries in 1839 escalated into the War of the Supremes, which 'raged for the next two years'; no border moved.
wars.note: The page gives no end date; the end year follows its 'next two years'. Panama also tried to break away 'unsuccessfully' in 1840.

wars.name: Colombian civil war of 1851
wars.outcome: A civil war in 1851 triggered by the Liberal reforms of President Jose Hilario Lopez; no border moved.

wars.name: Melo coup and civil war of 1854
wars.outcome: In April 1854 General Jose Maria Melo overthrew President Obando and 'proclaimed himself dictator', triggering another civil war; no border moved.

certainty.note: No boundary treaty is on the pages opened; the Amazon, Mosquito Coast and Brazilian frontiers are claims.

notes:
Two pages opened (the budget is 1-2): the Republic of New Granada article and Territorial evolution of Colombia (thin: no boundaries).

Cliopatria has no row for 1831-1833: the Gran Colombia row runs to 1833 with Venezuela and Ecuador inside (marked wrong in that dossier) and this row starts in 1834. The new keyframe fills 1831-1833 with the 1834 outline (the Gran Colombia dossier hands over Colombia and Panama only, 0.2 M km2 smaller than the outline); one of the two should yield. The infobox gives 20 October 1831 for the State of New Granada; the page does not mention an 1832 constitution.
The 1853 drop of 199,712 km2 (Brazil's Amazonas cells and Vaupes, Amazonas and Guainia) is not explained by any page opened (a gap-filler should open the Brazil-Colombia and Peru-Colombia boundary history and 'Caqueta'); the Panama secession attempts of 1840 and 1850 are given only as 'unsuccessful'. The 1832 Treaty of Pasto (Cauca turned over to New Granada, per the Ecuador page) and the Ecuador boundary are in the Ecuador dossier; no event is recorded because no page dates Ecuador's hold on Cauca. The Costa Rican, Nicaraguan and Venezuelan frontiers (the Mosquito Coast, the Guajira) are not on the pages opened.
